Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: MFA should be enabled for all IAM users
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether the AWS Identity and Access Management users have multi-factor authentication (MFA) enabled.

Recommendation.Text: To add MFA for IAM users, see "Enabling MFA devices for users in AWS" in the IAM User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning should be enabled
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning is enabled. For a standalone account, the control fails if Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning is disabled in the account. In a multi-account environment, the control fails if the delegated Inspector administrator account or any associated member account doesn't have Lambda standard scanning enabled.

Recommendation.Text: To enable Amazon Inspector Lambda standard scanning, see "Activating scans" in the Amazon Inspector User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Hardware MFA should be enabled for the root user
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether your AWS account is enabled to use a hardware multi-factor authentication (MFA) device to sign in with root user credentials.

Recommendation.Text: For information about enabling hardware MFA for the root user, see "Multi-factor authentication for an AWS account root user" in the IAM User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: CloudTrail should have encryption at-rest enabled
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether AWS CloudTrail is configured to use the server side encryption (SSE) AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer master key (CMK) encryption. The check will pass if the KmsKeyId is defined.

Recommendation.Text: To enable SSE-KMS encryption for CloudTrail log files, see "Update a trail to use a KMS key" in the AWS CloudTrail User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning should be enabled
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning is enabled. For a standalone account, the control fails if Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning is disabled in the account. In a multi-account environment, the control fails if the delegated Inspector administrator account or any associated member account doesn't have EC2 scanning enabled.

Recommendation.Text: To enable Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning, see "Activating scans" in the Amazon Inspector User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Unused IAM user credentials should be removed
Findings.Description: This control checks whether your IAM users have passwords or active access keys that were not used within the previous 90 days.

Recommendation.Text: When you view user information in the IAM console, there are columns for Access key age, Password age, and Last activity. If the value in any of these columns is greater than 90 days, make the credentials for those users inactive. You can also use "credential reports" to monitor users and identify those with no activity for 90 or more days. You can download credential reports in .csv format from the IAM console. After you identify the inactive accounts or unused credentials, deactivate them.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: IAM users' access keys should be rotated every 90 days or less
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether the active access keys are rotated within 90 days.

Recommendation.Text: To rotate access keys that are older than 90 days, see "Rotating access keys" in the IAM User Guide. Follow the instructions for any user with an Access key age greater than 90 days.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Security contact information should be provided for an AWS account.
Findings.Description: This control checks if an Amazon Web Services (AWS) account has security contact information. The control fails if security contact information is not provided for the account.

Recommendation.Text: To add an alternate contact as a security contact to your AWS account, see "Update the alternate contacts for your AWS account" in the AWS Account Management Reference Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Effects/Data Exposure
Findings.Title: EBS snapshots should not be configured to be publicly restorable
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon Elastic Block Store snapshots are configured to be publicly restorable. The control fails if Amazon EBS snapshots are configured to be restorable by all.

Recommendation.Text: To make a public EBS snapshot private, see "Share a snapshot" in the Amazon EC2 User Guide. For Actions, Modify permissions, choose Private.

Types: Effects/Data Exposure
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: EBS default encryption should be enabled
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) encryption is enabled by default. The control fails if EBS default encryption is not enabled.

Recommendation.Text: To configure default encryption for Amazon EBS volumes, see "Encryption by default" in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

ProductFields.aws/securityhub/annotation: EBS Encryption by default is not enabled.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: VPCs should be configured with an interface endpoint for ECR API
Findings.Description: This control checks whether a virtual private cloud (VPC) that you manage has an interface VPC endpoint for ECR API. The control fails if the VPC doesn't have an interface VPC endpoint for ECR API. This control evaluates resources in a single account.

Recommendation.Text: To configure a VPC endpoint, see "Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint" in the AWS PrivateLink Guide.

ProductFields.aws/securityhub/annotation: This VPC does not use a VPC endpoint for service ecr.api.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: VPCs should be configured with an interface endpoint for Systems Manager Incident Manager
Findings.Description: This control checks whether a virtual private cloud (VPC) that you manage has an interface VPC endpoint for Systems Manager Incident Manager. The control fails if the VPC doesn't have an interface VPC endpoint for Systems Manager Incident Manager. This control evaluates resources in a single account.

Recommendation.Text: To configure a VPC endpoint, see "Access an AWS service using an interface VPC endpoint" in the AWS PrivateLink Guide.

ProductFields.aws/securityhub/annotation: This VPC does not use a VPC endpoint for service ssm-incidents.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: EC2 VPC Block Public Access settings should block internet gateway traffic
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon EC2 VPC Block Public Access (BPA) settings are configured to block internet gateway traffic for all Amazon VPCs in the AWS account. The control fails if EC2 VPC BPA settings aren't configured to block internet gateway traffic. If the parameter `vpcBpaInternetGatewayBlockMode` is provided, the control passes only if the EC2 VPC BPA value for InternetGatewayBlockMode matches the parameter.

Recommendation.Text: To enable bi-directional BPA at the account level, see "Enable BPA bidirectional mode for your account" in the Amazon VPC User Guide. To enable ingress-only BPA, see "Change VPC BPA mode to ingress-only". To enable VPC BPA at the Organization level, see "Enable VPC BPA at the Organization level".

ProductFields.aws/securityhub/annotation: InternetGatewayBlockMode is not one of block-bidirectional or block-ingress.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Amazon EMR block public access setting should be enabled
Findings.Description: This control checks whether your account is configured with Amazon EMR block public access. The control fails if the block public access setting is not enabled or if any port other than 22 is allowed.

Recommendation.Text: To configure block public access for Amazon EMR, see "Using Amazon EMR block public access" in the Amazon EMR Management Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: IAM root user access key should not exist
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether the root user access key is available.

Recommendation.Text: To delete the root user access key, see "Deleting access keys for the root user" in the IAM User Guide. To delete the root user access keys from an AWS account in AWS GovCloud (US), see "Deleting my AWS GovCloud (US) account root user access keys" in the AWS GovCloud (US) User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: CloudTrail should be enabled and configured with at least one multi-Region trail that includes read and write management events
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks that there is at least one multi-region AWS CloudTrail trail includes read and write management events.

Recommendation.Text: To create a new multi-Region trail in CloudTrail, see "Creating a trail" in the AWS CloudTrail User Guide. Use the following values: |Field|Value| |---|---| |Additional settings, Log file validation|Enabled| |Choose log events, Management events, API activity|Read and Write. Clear check boxes for exclusions.| To update an existing trail, see "Updating a trail" in the AWS CloudTrail User Guide. In Management events, for API activity, choose Read and Write.

Findings.Title: VPCs should be configured with an interface endpoint for Docker Registry
Findings.Description: This control checks whether a virtual private cloud (VPC) that you manage has an interface VPC endpoint for Docker Registry. The control fails if the VPC doesn't have an interface VPC endpoint for Docker Registry. This control evaluates resources in a single account.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Password policies for IAM users should have strong configurations
Findings.Description: This control checks whether the account password policy for IAM users uses strong configurations. The control fails if the password policy doesn't use strong configurations. Unless you provide custom parameter values, Security Hub uses the default values mentioned in the preceding table. The 'PasswordReusePrevention' and 'MaxPasswordAge' parameters have no default value, so if you exclude these parameters, Security Hub ignores number of password rotations and password age when evaluating this control.

Recommendation.Text: To update your password policy, see "Setting an account password policy for IAM users" in the IAM User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: GuardDuty should be enabled
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether Amazon GuardDuty is enabled in your AWS account and region.

Recommendation.Text: To enable GuardDuty, see "Getting started with GuardDuty" in the Amazon GuardDuty User Guide.

Effects/Data Exposure
Findings.Title: S3 general purpose buckets should block public read access
Findings.Description: This control checks whether an Amazon S3 general purpose bucket permits public read access. It evaluates the block public access settings, the bucket policy, and the bucket access control list (ACL). The control fails if the bucket permits public read access.

Recommendation.Text: To block public read access on your Amazon S3 buckets, see "Configuring block public access settings for your S3 buckets" in the Amazon Simple Storage Service User Guide.

Findings.Title: CloudTrail log file validation should be enabled
Findings.Description: This AWS control checks whether CloudTrail log file validation is enabled.

Recommendation.Text: To enable CloudTrail log file validation, see "Enabling log file integrity validation for CloudTrail" in the AWS CloudTrail User Guide.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: Amazon EC2 should be configured to use VPC endpoints that are created for the Amazon EC2 service
Findings.Description: This control checks whether a service endpoint for Amazon EC2 is created for each VPC. The control fails if a VPC does not have a VPC endpoint created for the Amazon EC2 service.

Recommendation.Text: To create an interface endpoint to Amazon EC2 from the Amazon VPC console, see "Create a VPC endpoint" in the AWS PrivateLink Guide. For Service name, choose com.amazonaws.region.ec2. You can also create and attach an endpoint policy to your VPC endpoint to control access to the Amazon EC2 API. For instructions on creating a VPC endpoint policy, see "Create an endpoint policy" in the Amazon EC2 User Guide.

ProductFields.aws/securityhub/annotation: This VPC does not use a VPC endpoint for service ec2.

Types: Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Software and Configuration Checks/Industry and Regulatory Standards
Findings.Title: SSM Automation should have CloudWatch logging enabled
Findings.Description: This control checks whether Amazon CloudWatch logging is enabled for AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Automation. The control fails if CloudWatch logging isn't enabled for SSM Automation.

Recommendation.Text: For information about enabling CloudWatch logging for SSM Automation, see "Logging Automation action output with CloudWatch Logs" in the AWS Systems Manager User Guide.
